summary: Build site water balances, prioritize efficiency projects, and prepare credible disclosures. Explore this practical industrial water management course.
lede: Industrial water management training helps site and sustainability teams account for facility water use and identify practical improvements. For environmental and sustainability managers, plant and facilities leaders, and water engineers, it develops skills to build a site water balance, assess process efficiency options, and map operational and catchment risks. Participants also practise screening projects and preparing traceable inputs for water reporting using site data and spreadsheets.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for facility water use, process performance, catchment exposure, or corporate water reporting. This course is designed for: Environmental managers coordinating site water performance and environmental data. Sustainability managers preparing corporate water targets and disclosures. Plant managers balancing production requirements with facility water efficiency. Facilities managers reviewing water meters, utility use, and building systems. Water engineers developing site water balances and process efficiency options. Process engineers identifying water losses in production and cleaning operations. Extractives operations supervisors managing mine-site water use and operational risks. Water stewardship specialists assessing catchment context and site actions. Corporate reporting analysts compiling facility water data for GRI 303 disclosures. Capital project engineers screening water efficiency investments and reuse options.
outcomes: Alliance For Water Stewardship Standard Application
Water Meter Data Analysis In Excel
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with facility operations, environmental management, utility data, or process engineering is recommended. Prior water-accounting experience is helpful but not required. No coding or programming is required; advanced water-footprint and AI-assisted analysis topics are introduced at an overview or operational-use level.
